issues.rule_id: code-style §22 / consistency (MANIFEST.yml header '务必与 PR 正文一致')
issues.description: Committed documentation carries stale/inconsistent assertion counts that contradict the files updated by commit 891974cac4 and the actual sources. Independently counted from source: test.c has 9 CHECK() invocations (#define CHECK line excluded) -> 9; test_ohos_specific.c has 21 CHECK() invocations -> 21; test_consumer.c has 0 CHECK() macros (rc-based). test-report.md §0/§3.1/§3.2 and pr-body.md lines 24/54 therefore correctly report 'declared 30 / executed 26' (9+21=30 declared; 7+19=26 executed, confirmed line-by-line against reports/conan-create.log lines 2037-2085). But notes.md lines 88-90 still say 'test_rdma 9 / test_ohos_specific 20 / test_consumer 6', and test_package/MANIFEST.yml lines 85/89/93 declare assertions 9/20/6 (line 9 '合计...60 条断言'; lines 95-96 '断言总数 = ... 35 (9+20+6)', assertion_count: 60). So test_ohos_specific is under-reported as 20 (actual 21; the fix added one net CHECK replacing two sizeof assertions) and test_consumer is reported as 6 whereas test-report §3.3 says '5 处有效性检查'. MANIFEST.yml's own header states its tallies must match the PR body, which is now false. This is a documentation-consistency defect, not a forged test result: the tests genuinely ran (all pass, 0 failures).
issues.fix_suggestion: Update notes.md (lines 88-90) and test_package/MANIFEST.yml (lines 9, 85, 89, 93, 96) to the same audited numbers used in test-report.md/pr-body.md: test.c 9 declared / 7 executed, test_ohos_specific.c 21 declared / 19 executed, test_consumer.c rc-based (5 validity checks, no CHECK count). Recompute assertion_count accordingly (e.g. 25 upstream bitmap_test + 30 declared = 55, or state executed 51) so all committed docs agree.

issues.description: The replacement for the tautology 'sizeof(struct ibv_device *) > 0' is only partially non-trivial. Lines 84-85 initialize 'struct ibv_device **(*verbs_list)(int *) = ibv_get_device_list;' and 'struct ibv_context **(*cma_list)(int *) = rdma_get_devices;' then lines 89-90 assert 'verbs_list != NULL' / 'cma_list != NULL'. A function pointer initialized from a defined function's address can never compare equal to NULL, so these two runtime CHECKs are still trivially true. Their real (and verified) value is compile/link-time: the initializers force the linker to resolve ibv_get_device_list and rdma_get_devices declared by the two header families in one TU, and the code is compile-sane -- the pointer types match the upstream prototypes exactly (libibverbs/verbs.h:2301 'struct ibv_device **ibv_get_device_list(int *num_devices);' and librdmacm/rdma_cma.h:694 'struct ibv_context **rdma_get_devices(int *num_devices);'). Separately, test.c line 89 'CHECK(num_cma == 0 || rdma_ctxs != NULL, ...)' is vacuously satisfied in the only reachable OHOS path (num_cma == 0, no HCA), so it never validates the count/array relation at runtime.
issues.fix_suggestion: Assert a runtime-observable property instead of pointer-non-NULL (e.g. call through the pointer and check the returned element/count, or dlsym the symbol and assert it resolved), or add a comment stating the assertion's purpose is the link-time reference. Optionally tighten test.c:89 to something like 'CHECK(num_cma == 0 ? (rdma_ctxs == NULL || rdma_ctxs[0] == NULL) : rdma_ctxs != NULL, ...)'.

issues.rule_id: archive naming consistency (no explicit rule; observation)
issues.description: This PR introduces a second archive directory for the same upstream project. The same upstream linux-rdma/rdma-core already has 'archives/r/rdma-core/' with versions 56.1 and 61.0 (archives/r/rdma-core/manifest.yaml 'software: "rdma-core"', archives/r/rdma-core/commands.json name 'rdma-core'), while this PR adds 'archives/r/rdma/' (64.0) with 'software: "rdma"' (archives/r/rdma/manifest.yaml) and commands.json name 'rdma'. README.md line 4 justifies the name from the upstream CMakeLists set(PACKAGE_NAME "RDMA"). Internally consistent, but it fragments one upstream across two archive/package names (rdma/64.0 vs rdma-core/56.1|61.0), which may surprise downstream consumers and reviewers.
issues.fix_suggestion: Confirm with the maintainer whether the archive should remain 'rdma-core' for consistency with 56.1/61.0 (and the package ref 'rdma-core/64.0'), or explicitly document in README.md/notes.md why 64.0 intentionally renames the archive to 'rdma'. No code change is required if intentional.

issues.description: The headline counts are accurate (declared 30 / executed 26 / 0 failed), but the parenthetical attribution is imprecise: pr-body.md line 54 says the 4 unexecuted assertions are '位于有设备才进入的分支/循环内' (inside device-gated branches/loops). Independently, only 3 of the 4 are device-gated (test.c:54 and test.c:82 device loops; test_ohos_specific.c:236 T5 device loop); the 4th is test_ohos_specific.c:133, the 'rindex == NULL' branch of an if/else -- the runtime took the else branch (conan-create.log line 2065 'native rindex() agrees with strrchr()'), which is unrelated to device presence. test-report.md §3.2 states this correctly, so the two documents now disagree slightly.
issues.fix_suggestion: Reword pr-body.md line 54 to say the unexecuted assertions are '位于有设备才进入的循环/分支或 rindex 存在性 if/else 的未选分支内' (or simply defer the exact attribution to test-report.md §3.2).

summary: Verdict pass: P0=0, P1=0, P2=1, P3=3 (all non-blocking). Independently verified against the files (audit-input JSON matches the on-disk files byte-for-byte): (1) File boundary OK - merge-base..HEAD is exactly the 20 files in changed_files, all under archives/r/rdma/** and knowledge/drafts/E429-draft-98B5.*; no framework files, no SUMMARY.md, no other package, no .log; the 6 state files (.ci-result.json/.submit-state.json/.handoff.json/ci-metadata.json/.conan-verified/.build-closed) are untracked and gitignored (rule 24 satisfied). (2) Tests genuinely exercise the package (not shell tests): reports/conan-create.log lines 2035-2085 show 'Executing test' with RUN ./test_rdma, ./test_ohos_specific, ./test_consumer, each calling real public APIs (ibv_get_device_list/free/name/guid, rdma_get_devices/free_devices). (3) sha256 verified: 'd170d0265e1e5030c574c8613a1fecc047413282b94c2bc4cf2e99477d82ee93' equals sha256sum of the pinned tarball, and the URL is the official linux-rdma/rdma-core GitHub release (R39 OK). (4) The getpass fix is correct and complete: in compat/ohos-compat.h only the tcgetattr==0 block disables ECHO and it sets have_saved=1 first; the sole pre-disable early return (weak getpass present) never touches termios; the restore 'if (have_saved) tcsetattr(fd, TCSAFLUSH, &saved)' runs on every path that could have disabled echo - ECHO is now always restored. (5) test.c captures first_verbs at line 59, immediately after the first enumeration is freed and before the second call, so 'CHECK(num_verbs == first_verbs)' (line 65) is a real comparison, not the old tautology. (6) The test_ohos_specific.c function-pointer types match the upstream prototypes exactly, so the code is compile-sane. (7) Assertion recount (CHECK() invocations, macro definition excluded): test.c 9 declared, test_ohos_specific.c 21 declared, test_consumer.c 0 (rc-based); executed 7+19=26; 0 failures. The reported 30 declared / 26 executed / 0 failed is therefore ACCURATE and not under-reported. Residual risk: the same counts are stale in notes.md (88-90) and test_package/MANIFEST.yml (9/85/89/93/96), which still say 9/20/6 and assertion_count 60 (P2, documentation-only); two residual runtime CHECKs remain trivially true (P3); and the archive is named 'rdma' while the same upstream already exists as 'rdma-core' (56.1/61.0) (P3). None of these affect the pass verdict.
